sections.notes: Goal, roadmap, release criteria, and v0.0 technical-report framing have been reviewed and refreshed through the released v0.0 wording pass.

Public app/task expansion, private holdout aggregate counts, the combined vulnerable/control mix, the first project-management multi-step workflow wave, and the generated public task-quality matrix have review coverage. This section is reviewed; the remaining current live HTTP tool-agent rerun is tracked by the baseline credibility gate.

Scorer, runner, request-log correlation, live tool-agent execution proof on both public and private holdouts, tool-agent plan/probe artifact summary telemetry, and the distinction between scorer-derived and adapter-reported finding totals have complete review coverage. Public and protected paths also share the same false-positive versus false-report semantics. This section is v0-ready.

Review coverage for registry, leaderboard validators, frozen v0.0 46-task public model summaries, the repeated frozen v0.0 46-task public tool-agent baseline, chart readability, and benchmark fingerprint comparability is complete. The active 54-task split has an internally reviewed repeated no-tools Qwen family and a locally reviewed Claude Haiku 4.5 promotion awaiting commit/push and exact-head CI; Qwen retains explicit task-level adapter and runner failure diagnostics, while Haiku has complete zero-failure artifacts and a repeated authorized-allow false report. The historical 49-task split has five repeated no-tools model families plus one repeated live HTTP tool-agent family with full target-request correlation; those rows are stale for the active 54-task split. This supports Level 1/v0 baseline credibility and limited current 54-task public diagnostics, not stable current cross-model comparison, hosted leaderboard readiness, v1-scale community status, or private-holdout model ranking claims.

Holdout workflow, anti-gaming checks, redacted private-pack evidence, route/decoy variant counts, and private execution have review coverage. The newer private no-tools row is source-backed and release-candidate eligible because its benchmark fingerprint provenance is runner-emitted; the older reconstructed historical row remains non-eligible. One host-isolated private tool-agent run adds count-level target-request correlation; it is execution-availability evidence, not a repeated or eligible tool-agent leaderboard row.

CI, privacy scan, baseline gates, local private-holdout gates, protected no-tools evidence, and one private tool-agent run with count-level target correlation are verified. The release-wiring and report-review passes refreshed README, roadmap, release notes, launch-report, release-evidence wording, and technical-report framing for released v0.0. Hosted leaderboard and v1/community claims remain future work.
